name: Stella Choi
life: “I still remember catching my school coat in the gap between our gardens.” On Sunday, near the blocks below Foundry Lofts, Stella checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
voice: I used to squeeze through the gap to see my best friend. The new gate needs to be high enough for our grown-up heads.
appearance: Stella is easy to recognize by dark brown curls cut close behind the ears and a long face and high cheekbones. Usually dressed in a rust-colored canvas coat with a thin silver ring worn on a cord, Stella rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket when listening.
personality: Stella finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
agenda: To leave room for two former children now grown.
family: Fern Lin is Stella’s cousin. Stella gets to change the plan. Fern offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *A call heard twice*, Fern says, “I took the second call and inherited the trust the first voice had built.”
connections: Charlie Black. The old childhood gap is a better starting point for the survey than the center of the hedge.

reactions.response: Stella asks the household members who will use the garden how they want to live in it now.

reactions.situation: A driver splashes a market worker and tries to laugh it off
reactions.response: Stella helps shift the damp stock and makes sure the worker gets to describe the loss without interruption.

reactions.situation: When somebody waves from across traffic
reactions.response: Stella waits at the corner to hear their voice and give them a proper answer.
